extracted.intended_audience: hospitals, CJR-X participants, hospital administrators, Medicare payment model stakeholders and commenters
extracted.subtask_description: Proposed regulatory methodology for constructing, risk-adjusting, and reconciling episode target prices under the CJR-X bundled payment model, including trend factors, discounts, low-volume rules, normalization, and reconciliation timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective trend factor
rubrics_metrics.description: Defined as the multiplier incorporated into the preliminary target price to estimate changes in spending patterns between the baseline period and the performance year (proposed §512.605). Preliminary target prices would incorporate a prospective trend factor for each MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type and region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to predict future spending for pricing stability. CJR-X proposes to use an approach similar to TEAM's prospective trend (but without TEAM's two trend years) so that the shared baseline data aligns with the trend construction. CMS seeks comment on defining and applying the prospective trend factor and alternative trend constructions to increase accuracy and mitigate the ratchet effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retrospective trend factor (capped +/-3%)
rubrics_metrics.description: A +/−3 percent capped 'retrospective trend factor' (proposed §512.605 and §512.645(f)) applied at reconciliation as the multiplier incorporated into the reconciliation target price to estimate realized changes in spending patterns during the performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modeled on TEAM's approach with a +/-3% cap to balance accuracy and predictability. CMS considered +/-5% and +/-10% but chose a narrower cap to improve stability and reduce disproportionate impact from unforeseen performance-year spending shifts. CMS seeks comment on applying this retrospective factor and the cap level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discount factor (2% to benchmark)
rubrics_metrics.description: Apply a 2 percent discount factor to the benchmark price to serve as Medicare's portion of reduced expenditures from the episode (proposed §512.640(b)(8)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is lower than the 3% discount used in some prior models; CMS considered 3%, 1.5%, 1%, and no discount, and considered linking discount magnitude to baseline variability or phased reductions, but did not propose those alternatives. CMS seeks comment on the 2% discount and alternative discount approaches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-volume hospital threshold and treatment
rubrics_metrics.description: Define 'low-volume hospital' as a hospital with fewer than 31 LEJR episodes performed during the applicable baseline period (proposed §512.605); low-volume hospitals would be excluded from reconciliation for the performance year (proposed §512.640(a)(4)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As in BPCI Advanced, hospitals failing to meet the minimum volume would not trigger CJR-X episodes or receive a target price; episodes at those hospitals during the performance year would be excluded from regional benchmark calculations but would count toward future baselines as the baseline window shifts. CMS considered but did not propose performance-year minimum episode thresholds (e.g., <10 or <15) due to concerns about steering/ program integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary target prices: timing and contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary target price is the target price provided to the participant prior to the start of the performance year and subject to adjustment at reconciliation (proposed §512.640(b)(9)). CMS would provide preliminary target prices prior to the start of each performance year, for example by the end of November prior to the performance year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary target prices would be based on regional episode spending during the baseline period and would incorporate a prospective trend factor, a discount factor, and a prospective normalization factor. CMS will provide these in a form/manner specified by CMS to enable participant estimation of episode-level target prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment methodology (TEAM-based, MS-DRG level)
rubrics_metrics.description: CJR-X proposes to use the same risk adjustment methodology and variables used in TEAM (proposed §512.645 and §512.605), calculating multipliers at the MS-DRG level and providing separate sets of risk adjustment multipliers for each MS-DRG episode type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Risk adjust at the hospital level (bed size, safety net) and beneficiary level (180-day lookback for CJR-X HCC count, age bracket, beneficiary economic risk factor, and certain condition/HCC indicators). Coefficients are calculated prospectively prior to each performance year using baseline data and held constant at reconciliation, and participants receive multipliers prior to the performance year to estimate target prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prospective normalization factor (with +/-5% reconciliation adjustment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a 'prospective normalization factor' in preliminary target prices that would be subject to a limited adjustment at reconciliation based on observed case mix, up to +/−5 percent, to construct the final normalization factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This aligns with TEAM's approach to provide more predictability for participants while allowing limited correction at reconciliation. CMS intends to include the full baseline period in constructing the prospective normalization factor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beneficiary-level risk adjustment variables and lookback window
rubrics_metrics.description: Use beneficiary-level variables including age brackets (<65, 65-74, 75-84, 85+), a CJR-X HCC count constructed using a 180-day lookback of FFS Medicare claims, and a beneficiary economic risk adjustment (binary) that accounts for area deprivation, LIS eligibility, or full Medicaid eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 180-day lookback was adopted (changed from 90-day in TEAM proposal). The beneficiary economic risk adjustment is binary (yes/no) if any of the three criteria are met as of the first day of the episode. CMS also adds episode-specific condition/HCC indicators for LEJR (extensive list provided) to capture condition-specific spending impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific HCCs and condition indicators for LEJR risk adjustment
rubrics_metrics.description: Include certain HCCs and clinical indicators in the LEJR beneficiary risk adjustment, e.g., HCC 17, 36, 37, 48, 125-127, 151, 155, 199, 224-226, 238, 253, 267, 280, 326-327, 383, 402, and clinical procedure flags (ankle, partial hip, partial knee, total hip, total knee, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These binary risk adjustments (yes=1, no=0) reflect the differential effects of specific chronic conditions and prior services (e.g., prior post-acute care use, disability as original reason for Medicare enrollment) on episode spending and are intended to improve target price accuracy for LEJR episodes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospital-level risk adjustment: bed size and safety net
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjust target prices at the hospital level using a hospital bed size risk adjustment factor and a safety net risk adjustment factor (proposed §512.645).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS proposes a binary safety net definition: a hospital in the top 25th percentile in their region for percentage of FFS LEJR inpatient episodes provided to dually eligible beneficiaries during the baseline. CMS considered segmenting into 3+ groups but declined due to sample size/accuracy concerns and seeks comment on the binary safety net proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation approach for risk adjustment coefficients
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate risk adjustment coefficients prospectively prior to each performance year (using baseline data) via a regression model and hold them constant at reconciliation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CJR-X will use an approach similar to TEAM (and distinct from BPCI Advanced's more complex compound log-normal model) to balance precision and interpretability; coefficients are shared with participants so they can estimate episode-level target prices prior to the performance year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual reconciliation (one per performance year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct one annual reconciliation that compares performance year episode spending to reconciliation target prices to determine reconciliation payments or repayments (proposed §512.650).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS believes one annual reconciliation provides regular performance feedback while minimizing administrative burden compared to more frequent reconciliations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation timing: ~6 months after performance year end
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose to conduct the annual reconciliation roughly 6 months after the end of the performance year (to allow for claims runout).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS cites internal claim completeness data (e.g., 98.71% of IP claims received and 89.96% considered final by 6 months) to justify 6 months as sufficient for a nearly complete picture of performance year spending across claim types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality adjustment integrated into reconciliation
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate participant quality performance into the reconciliation calculation by adjusting the reconciliation target price for quality based on the participant's CQS, constructed from performance on proposed quality measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quality adjustment details referenced in section X.C.2.e.; the reconciliation target price will be adjusted for quality performance before computing NPRA and applying stop-loss/stop-gain limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reconciliation calculation steps: NPRA, stop-loss/stop-gain, post-episode spending
rubrics_metrics.description: Calculate difference between aggregated reconciliation target price across episodes and actual episode spending to create raw NPRA; apply stop-loss/stop-gain limits to determine NPRA; subtract post-episode spending when applicable to determine reconciliation payment or repayment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This outlines the high-level reconciliation flow. See related sections for definitions of related services, performance years, and preliminary target price construction. CMS will apply episode-level risk adjustment, update normalization factor, and update trend factor during reconciliation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exclusion of setting-specific update factors from preliminary target prices
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered but is not proposing to include update factors that reflect Medicare payment system updates (IPPS, OPPS, PFS, HH PPS, MEI, IRF PPS, SNF PPS) in the preliminary target price because doing so would create multiple preliminary target prices during a performance year and reduce pricing stability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS is interested in capturing payment system updates and proposes an alternative in another section to update the preliminary target price when constructing the reconciliation target price while avoiding sharing update factors that require participants to manage multiple preliminary target prices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of retrospective adjustments to address coding/practice changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Retrospective trend adjustments are used to account for significant spending changes arising from coding guidance or practice pattern changes that prospective trending cannot capture (example: FY2016 inpatient CHF coding change shifting patients from MS-DRG 292 to 291 without clinical change).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS modified prior models to include retrospective adjustments because fully prospective trend factors could not account for coding changes; these retrospective adjustments were initially subject to wide guardrails (+/-10%) and subsequently narrowed based on feedback (to +/-5% then proposed +/-3%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of administrative trend approaches to mitigate ratchet effect
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS considered using an administrative trend component (e.g., Accountable Care Prospective Trend (ACPT)) to insulate a portion of the prospective update from retrospective savings-driven effects and requests comment on using such administrative trending for episode-based models.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative trends may address ratchet effects by decoupling some trending from observed FFS spending, but CMS notes concerns that administrative trends may not capture episode-specific trends, potentially leading to misestimation of preliminary target prices for episode-based payment models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk adjustment granularity: MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type level (not region)
rubrics_metrics.description: Risk adjustment multipliers will be calculated at the MS-DRG (or MS-DRG/HCPCS episode type) level rather than MS-DRG/HCPCS/region level because subdividing further into regions could produce insufficient volume for accurate multipliers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reflects a tradeoff between granularity and statistical reliability; CMS considered MS-DRG/HCPCS/region but concluded low volumes would undermine accuracy for certain episode types/regions.
